lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the northern kingdom of Israel, King Ahab had turned away from the LORD. Queen Jezebel had promoted the worship of Baal, and the nation was being led deeper into idolatry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Elijah the Tishbite appeared before Ahab. He came with a warning from the living God.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives—the God I serve—there will be no dew or rain unless the LORD gives the word.

choices.label: Stand boldly on God's word
choices.note: Elijah's message is clear: Israel's drought is a direct challenge to Baal, the god they claimed controlled the rain.

choices.label: Feel the weight of the king's threat
choices.note: Elijah is brave, but the story will soon show that even a courageous prophet can become afraid.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Leave here. Go east and hide beside the Kerith Ravine. You will drink from the brook, and I have commanded ravens to provide food for you there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elijah obeyed. Morning and evening the ravens brought him bread and meat, and he drank from the brook.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But after a time the brook dried up. The drought had reached even the place where God had provided for Elijah.
